blocks.title: Missed call at 7:42, {{booked job}} by 7:44
blocks.description: One customer, one thread. The conversation moves from a missed call to SMS to WhatsApp, and the customer repeats nothing. A job sits in your booking software at the end.

turns.text: Missed call from a mobile number. Both crews left at seven and nobody is in the office yet.
turns.action: Logs the call as a new lead, and queues a text-back before the caller reaches the next listing.

turns.text: Hi, this is Bright Home Cleaning — sorry we missed you. I can help right here. What kind of clean do you need?
Move-out clean, 3 bed 2 bath in Northgate. Friday if you have it.
Northgate is in our area. A 3 bed / 2 bath move-out is a flat $240. Friday I have 10 a.m. or 2 p.m. — which suits you?
turns.action: Checks the service area, applies your rate card, and reads Friday crew availability from the calendar.

turns.text: 10 a.m. works. Sending photos — the kitchen is rough, is that extra?
Looked at them — that kitchen is inside the flat rate, no surprise charge. You are booked for Friday at 10 a.m. Want the same crew every two weeks?
turns.action: Holds the slot, writes the job to your scheduling tool, and offers a recurring plan.

blocks.outcomeNote: The customer accepted the biweekly plan in the same thread. Nobody in your office touched any of it.

blocks.title: Frequently Asked Questions About AI Receptionist

items.question: How is an AI receptionist for cleaning companies different from the answering service we already pay for?
items.answer: An answering service takes a message, and your office manager still calls the customer back. The agent runs the lead from first ring to confirmed job, with live access to your booking software and calendar. It works on SMS, voice, web, email, and WhatsApp.

items.question: What does the agent handle, and what does it hand to a human?
items.answer: The agent answers calls and texts, qualifies the lead, quotes standard scopes, and books the crew. It also sends reminders, follows up on quotes, and offers the recurring plan. Your estimator handles commercial walk-throughs, and the agent escalates with the full history.

items.question: How does it handle one-time deep cleans versus recurring customers?
items.answer: One-time scopes get an instant flat rate and a same-week slot. Recurring customers pick a cadence, save a payment method, and get renewal reminders. The agent offers the recurring plan in the booking conversation.

items.question: What about commercial accounts that need a walk-through estimate?
items.answer: The agent flags commercial requests and captures square footage, frequency, scope, and service area. It books a walk-through with your estimator, or quotes from your pricing matrix when the scope fits a template. Portfolio requests route straight to a human.

items.question: Does it work for our specific cleaning type — residential maid, commercial, janitorial, vacation-rental turnover, post-construction, or specialty?
items.answer: Yes, the funnel is the same for every cleaning type: capture the scope, quote, book, and follow up. Only the variables change: bedrooms for residential, square footage for commercial. You set them once in the template.

items.question: Who owns the customer data and conversation records?
items.answer: You do. Call recordings, transcripts, photos, and CRM records live in your account. Acme never uses them to train public AI models, and you can export or delete them.

items.question: What affects how long deployment takes?
items.answer: Three things: your intake and pricing rules, the systems the agent writes to, and the channels you launch. An SMS-only start goes faster than full voice, web, email, and WhatsApp coverage. Most operators go live in five to fifteen working days.

items.question: What happens to my speed-to-lead and missed-call rate?
items.answer: First touch drops from hours to seconds. Cleaning operators miss 25 to 40% of inbound calls, and the evening and weekend peak is the worst of it. The agent answers those live, or recovers them by text inside 60 seconds.

items.question: How do credits map to call and message volume?
items.answer: Each agent action draws a set credit cost. A conversation turn, a booking lookup, a calendar write, a CRM update, and an outbound message all have a rate. A text-only intake runs roughly 8 to 15 turns.

items.question: Can the platform extend beyond lead handling once we’re running?
items.answer: Yes. The same canvas runs cleaner recruiting, customer service on active jobs, supply ordering, and contract-renewal outreach. Most operators start with lead handling, then add agents as confidence grows.
